summary: Resumed after the session limit kill of 16:45. The previous run had already written every item in code; this run read the five owner files, compiled them (SetupAndCompile PASS, 12 shaders, 0 failure), built Build/biome-electric-liquid, ran every acceptance check on that build and finished the open work. (1) Electric current packet: halo opacity 0.8, head quad 1.5 x (1.2 x 0.69 u) with a faster forward falloff so it never runs past the front, an LDR-safe spark star (0.1 u solid white center in a white-blue core below luma 235) for the 0.5 u glint, spark dots capped at 1.1 x the player color (no white core), plus the actors package's request: the electric chevron fill is capped at 0.8 linear so the home chevron no longer reads white beside the packet. CutDroplets, Medium, 540x960, pink human (reference conditions): packet luma >= 235 area 3.9 x the largest pearl (Gate B 1.65 x); dead-cable dots keep their color. (2) Electric fill: the discharge follows the smooth wide contour field and the clamped reveal age only gates it; the cell staircases along the fill edge are gone, the discharge still spreads from the return point in about 0.27 s and the hex pattern pulses once; a short hard cut remains where the band meets older territory (needs a Gather, which the target 2.0 Shader Graph forward pass cannot use, or a reveal texture change). (3) perf-04 and perf-06: dynamic branches around the plasma surface, rim and micro arcs (electric) and around the ground and puddle shading (liquid), every derivative and implicit-LOD sample outside them, fetch counts unchanged. perfslope (Medium, uncapped, ms per Mpix): electric 2.43, 16.5 % below the 2.91 baseline (Gate B in the same session 3.14), PASS; liquid 2.48 against the target 1.86 (Gate B in the same session 2.24): no measurable gain, acceptance not met. Probe hash 246577239DE179C4 on every run. (4) Liquid crease: the contact of two puddles is a soft dark groove, isolated bright specks in the coral-lilac contact 35 -> 0 (Medium) and 45 -> 0 (High). Liquid DevShots otherwise unchanged. EditMode 491 tests, 0 failure (10 new WaveC_ tests, including a compile of every owned graph's forward pass for GLES3x and Direct3D 11). Found on the way: the URP Unlit Shader Graph forward pass is '#pragma target 2.0' on every platform, so Gather paths guarded by SHADER_TARGET >= 45 never run (this affects FireComposite too).
api_additions: ElectricFx.PacketHaloOpacity (public const float 0.8) and ElectricFx.PacketHalfSize (public static readonly Vector2 (1.2, 0.69)): the packet halo opacity and head quad half size, read by the tests

ElectricOverlay.hlsl defines: PIOE_GLINT_WHITE 0.1 (world radius of the spark star's white center), PIOE_GLINT_CENTER 1.6, PIOE_GLINT_BLUE (0.30, 0.62, 1.0), PIOE_PACKET_AHEAD 2.25, PIOE_CHEVRON_MAX 0.8
ElectricBead.hlsl: PIOE_DOT_PEAK 1.1; ElectricComposite.hlsl: PIOE_FILL_AGE 0.4; LiquidComposite.hlsl: PIO_CREASE_DARK 0.25
contract_issues: 25.4 Fill: the electric discharge now rides the advancing contour of the fill (a band about 0.14 to 0.8 u behind it, from the wide relief field) and the reveal age only gates it on and off; it no longer floods the whole freshly revealed area. Suggested wording: 'a crackling discharge of branching lightning rides the advancing front of the fill from the return point (0.25 s), then the hex pattern pulses once'.

25.4 Cut and 25.5: the dead-cable spark dots (ElectricBead small beads) peak at 1.1 x the player color and never clip to white; the current packet has a 0.8 opacity white-blue halo and a 1.5 x head; the electric glint (ElectricOverlay shape 3) is a 0.1 u solid white center in a white-blue core that stays below sRGB luma 235 without bloom, designed for the 0.5 u glint half size set by the actors package; the electric chevron (shape 2) fill is capped at 0.8 linear.

12.2 item 4 and the plan's shader rule 4: the URP Unlit Shader Graph target generates one subshader whose Universal Forward pass is '#pragma target 2.0' on every platform (only its GBuffer pass is 4.5). SHADER_TARGET is 20 in every composite, bead and overlay forward pass, so code guarded by 'PLATFORM_SUPPORT_GATHER && SHADER_TARGET >= 45' never runs, on Windows as on Android. The rule should read 'the forward pass compiles for Direct3D 11 and GLES3' and the contract should not count on Gather in Shader Graph composites.

25.2 (only if the residual of visuals-reveal-age-staircase must go): removing the last hard cut where the electric discharge meets older territory needs either four point fetches of _PIO_RevealTime (beyond the 12.2 item 4 budget) or a reveal texture whose values are already clamped ages (for example a second RHalf channel 'age at the last write, saturating', written by TerritoryField), which changes 25.2.

items.evidence: Code: ElectricFx.DrawChase draws the white-blue halo at PacketHaloOpacity 0.8 (was 0.4) and the packet head quad at PacketHalfSize 1.2 x 0.69 u (1.5 x the B-2 0.8 x 0.46); ElectricOverlay shape 10 falls off PIOE_PACKET_AHEAD = 2.25 times faster ahead of the head, so it reaches past the front exactly as far as before (V7). ElectricOverlay shape 3 (the glint the actors package draws at 0.5 u half size): a solid white center of PIOE_GLINT_WHITE = 0.1 u world radius (through UV0.z) at value 1.6 (bloom on High only), around it a white-blue core lerp(albedo, (0.30, 0.62, 1.0), 0.75) x (0.85 to 1.1) that stays below luma 235 without bloom, jagged rays unchanged. ElectricBead small-bead branch: no white core any more, color = col x min(1.1, core x 1.1 + glow x 1.15). ElectricOverlay shape 2 (needs of the actors package): the chevron fill lost its 1.15 to 1.4 boost and is capped at 0.8 linear. EditMode: WaveC_PacketHalo_IsStronger_AndHeadIsOneAndAHalfTimesLarger, WaveC_SparkStar_IsLdrSafe_WhiteCenterOnly, WaveC_SparkDots_NeverClipToWhite_ForAnyElectricColor (all 4 electric colors x 1.1 stay below luma 235 and keep a channel below 0.5), WaveC_HomeChevron_IsCappedBelowWhite. Acceptance on Build/biome-electric-liquid, DevShot -quality medium 540x960 electric CutDroplets, measured with docs/waveC/biome-electric-liquid/tools/packet_measure.py (luma >= 235 pixels in a 10 px disc on the packet head and a 15 px disc on each pearl): run with the coral-pink human (the reference conditions of docs/waveC/visuals/zoom_electric_cut_540_high.png): packet 214 vs largest pearl 55 = 3.89 x (Gate B build Build/Windows, same settings: 107 vs 65 = 1.65 x), PASS (>= 1.5 x); the rival pearl shows 2. Dead-cable dots: in the cable strip above the yellow wire, white pixels (every channel > 200) 31 -> 5 (the 5 are shed spark streaks, not dots), saturated red pixels 36 -> 121, max luma of the dots below the old white cores; crop crops/electric_deadcable_dots_540_medium_gateB_vs_new_pink.png shows red dots where Gate B had white-cored ones. Final build run (the shared saved color preference had switched the human to electric yellow): the literal luma ratio reads 0.72 because the saturated yellow orb body itself clips to luma 236; counting near-white pixels (every channel >= 230) the packet leads 173 vs 53 = 3.26 x (pink run 4.48 x, Gate B 1.78 x); the home chevron has 0 bright pixels (218 in the pink run before the cap, 91 at Gate B). Crops: crops/electric_cut_540_medium_gateB_vs_new_pink.png, crops/electric_packet_540_medium_new_pink_8x.png, crops/electric_cut_540_medium_final_yellow.png; shots under shots/e_med_new (pink, before the chevron cap), shots/e_med_final (yellow, final), shots/e_med_old (Gate B).

Code (ElectricComposite.hlsl): one bilinear _PIO_RevealTime fetch as before; the age is clamped to [0, PIOE_FILL_AGE = 0.4 s] and only drives gate = 1 - smoothstep(0.05, 0.32, age) and the one hex pulse (0.12 to 0.40 s); WHERE the discharge shows comes from the smooth wide relief field: band = smoothstep(0.70, 0.80, wide) x (1 - smoothstep(0.95, 0.9992, wide)) (about 0.14 to 0.8 u behind the contour) and a crest at wide 0.80 (about 0.2 u), as LiquidComposite's ripple does. TerritoryField and the -1000 sentinel untouched. EditMode WaveC_ElectricFill_ClampsTheAge_AndDrawsNoEdgeFromIt and WaveC_Composites_KeepTheirFetchCount (one reveal fetch, 10 fetch sites as in B-2). Acceptance, DevShot electric 1080x1200 (default tier) MidFill on Build/biome-electric-liquid vs Gate B: the 7.5 px square steps along the bottom of the discharge zone and along its top boundary are gone, the band follows the contour smoothly (crops/electric_fill1080_gateB_vs_new.png, crops/electric_fill1080_leftedge_gateB_vs_new.png). Window-grab sequence, 540x960 High, about 20 fps (crops/electric_fill_sequence_540_high_new.png vs ..._gateB.png): the band, its crackling branches and ElectricFx's bolts spread from the return point between 8.61 s and 8.88 s (about 0.27 s), the hex lines of the new area pulse once around 9.2 to 9.3 s, everything is faded by 9.33 s. Not fixed: where the band crosses into older territory (the two junctions of the new area with the old territory) it is still cut by a hard cell-aligned corner, one step about 35 px long at 1080 width that lasts the 0.3 s fade (luma 113 -> 155 in one pixel at y = 829; crops/electric_fill1080_junction_residual_8x.png, crops/electric_fill_junction_fade_540_new.png). Cause: bilinear filtering mixes a fresh reveal time with the old cell's -1000 (or older time), so the clamped age snaps within one pixel. Tried in this run: one Gather of the reveal texture with each age clamped before the bilinear weights (the FireComposite scheme, same fetch count). It changed nothing on the build: the Shader Graph Unlit forward pass compiles at '#pragma target 2.0' on every platform, so the SHADER_TARGET >= 45 guard is never true. Reverted as dead code. Removing the residual needs four point fetches or a 25.2 reveal texture change (contract_issues). Also note the discharge now reads calmer than at B-2: a band riding the front instead of a flash over the whole fresh area.

Code (ElectricComposite.hlsl): the ground (circuit board, halo) runs in [branch] if (cT < 1), the plasma hex tiling, flow noise and sin, the surface, rim, discharge sweep and short circuit run in [branch] if (cT > 0) with color = lerp(ground, surface, cT) unchanged (cT is exactly 0 off the territory and exactly 1 inside); the micro arcs run in [branch] if (tj > 0.12 && tj < 0.75) with the AA width arcAA = 1.4 x fwidth(tj) + 2 x pix taken outside; the hex lines use an analytic AA width (PIOE_HexEdge) so no derivative runs inside a branch; the bolt quads were not shrunk (deferred). EditMode WaveC_OwnedShaders_NoDerivativeOrImplicitLodSampleInsideDynamicBranches (parses every [branch] block, nested ones included, and every helper that uses a derivative; at least 7 branches in ElectricComposite) and WaveC_OwnedGraphsCompileOnEverySubshader (forward pass compiled for GLES3x and Direct3D 11). Electric DevShots unchanged at a glance (crops/electric_pocket_540_medium_gateB_vs_new.png; only the time-random hopping arcs differ). Per-pixel slope (tools/verify.ps1 -Steps perfslope, release probe, -quality medium -fps 1000, windowed 1080x1200 and 540x600, 2 rounds, best avgMs per size): Build/biome-electric-liquid electric 2.43 ms per Mpix (1080x1200 3.55 ms, 540x600 1.19 ms), that is 16.5 % below the plan baseline 2.91 (PASS, target <= 2.47); the Gate B build measured right after it in the same session on a quiet machine gives electric 3.14 (4.37 / 1.32 ms), so the change is -22.6 % like for like. All runs PASS with probe hash 246577239DE179C4 (sim unchanged). Logs: perf/perfslope_biome-electric-liquid.log (15 runs, 4 retried because another player or a Unity editor shared the machine; electric 540x600 flagged noisy x1.3) and perf/perfslope_gateB_same_session.log (12 runs, none shared).

Code (LiquidComposite.hlsl): PIO_Ground, the vignette and the ground shadow run in [branch] if (cT < 1); PIO_ShadeLiquid, PIO_InnerStreak, the crease and the ripple lift run in [branch] if (cT > 0); color = lerp(ground, puddle, cT) unchanged; the wobble, every fwidth and the pocket and actor blocks stay outside; the territory shadow tap is skipped where cT = 1 (it only fed the ground shadow), which saves a fetch inside puddles and adds none. EditMode: the branch and fetch tests above (13 fetch sites as in B-2). DevShots 540x960 High and Medium (menu, MidFill, PocketPending, CutDroplets) against the Gate B build with the same settings: identical apart from the crease (item below) and the other packages' changes (UI menu, actors glint and chevron glow): crops/liquid_pocket_540_high_gateB_vs_new.png, crops/liquid_midfill_540_medium_gateB_vs_new.png, crops/liquid_cut_540_high_gateB_vs_new.png; V1-V8 look kept (relief, streaks, drop shadow, ripple, pocket stripes). Acceptance NOT met: perfslope liquid 2.48 ms per Mpix on Build/biome-electric-liquid (1080x1200 3.60 ms, 540x600 1.19 ms) against the target <= 1.86 (12 % below 2.11); the Gate B build in the same session gives 2.24 (3.49 / 1.31 ms). At the large size the two builds are within noise (3.60 vs 3.49 ms; my only quiet 1080x1200 run was round 2, round 1 shared the machine with another player 3 times), so the branches bring no measurable gain on Iris Xe in the probe scene. Probable reason (not profiled): the per-pixel cost of the liquid composite sits mostly elsewhere, in the 7 Medium fetches and in the woven-grain ground (3 value noises), which still runs on the ground pixels that dominate the probe view. Logs as in perf-04. Hash 246577239DE179C4 on every run.

Code (LiquidComposite.hlsl only): crease = 1 - smoothstep(creaseCore, creaseCore + max(0.5 creaseCore, 2 fwCrease), gap), where creaseCore is the gap across one relief texel and fwCrease the sum of the two channels' own fwidths (fwidth(gap) collapses in the 2 x 2 quads that straddle the V-shaped contact, which left every other quad uncreased); inside the puddle branch the shaded color is blended toward a flat-lit groove (no streak, specular or Fresnel rim) darkened by PIO_CREASE_DARK 0.25; the relief gradient fed to the lighting is clamped to h0 / (2 pix) and the actor normal uses the same clamped gradient (no seam). EditMode WaveC_LiquidCrease_FlattensAndCapsTheLitSlope. Acceptance, DevShot liquid 540x960 PocketPending on Build/biome-electric-liquid vs Gate B, at the coral-lilac contact (the saffron-lilac pair of the reference is coral-lilac in today's color setup): a soft dark groove, no alternating white and dark single pixels (crops/liquid_crease_540_medium_gateB_vs_new.png, crops/liquid_crease_540_high_gateB_vs_new.png). Isolated bright specks (luma 40 above both horizontal neighbours) in the contact strip: Medium 35 -> 0, High 45 -> 0. V1-V8 kept (see perf-06).

open_issues: visuals-reveal-age-staircase residual: one hard cell-aligned cut where the electric discharge band meets older territory near each junction of a new area (about 35 px at 1080 width, during the 0.3 s fade). Needs a contract decision (contract_issues, 25.2) or acceptance as is.

perf-06 acceptance not met: liquid 2.48 ms per Mpix on my build against the 1.86 target (Gate B 2.24 in the same session, within noise at 1080x1200). The branches are correct and visually neutral but give no measurable gain in the probe scene. A real liquid gain would need cheaper ground shading (the woven grain) or fewer fetches, which touches the V1-V8 look and the 12.2 item 4 budget: a decision for the gate or a later wave. The perf numbers come from a shared machine (4 of my 15 runs were retried); the gate's quiet-machine run should confirm them.

DevShot takes the human's color from the saved preference, which other agents' runs changed during the wave (coral, then saffron, then electric yellow in this run). Luma-threshold acceptance checks depend on it: with an electric-yellow human the saturated yellow alone reaches luma 236. The gate should pin the color (or use the near-white count of tools/packet_measure.py).

The electric fill discharge is calmer than at Gate B (a band riding the advancing front plus the bolts, instead of a bright flash over the whole fresh area). It matches the plan's fix and contract 25.4, but it is a visible change of feel worth a look at the gate.

Transparency: this session's scratchpad is shared by the wave's agents; at 18:55 I overwrote a file named devshot.ps1 there (I did not know it existed); its replacement is a working DevShot launcher with a similar purpose. My own files are under scratchpad/bel/.
needs: biome-fire (Assets/Resources/Shaders/FireComposite.hlsl): PIO_FIRE_GATHER is never defined in the shipped shader. The Shader Graph Unlit forward pass is '#pragma target 2.0' on every platform (URP UniversalTarget CorePragmas.Forward), so SHADER_TARGET is 20 on Windows too, and the Gather reveal ages and the Gather relief normal are compiled out everywhere: the bilinear fallback is what runs. I saw the same with an identical Gather in ElectricComposite (no change at all on the build). The fire fill staircase acceptance should be checked on a build, and WaveC_FireGraphsCompileOnEverySubshader only ever compiles the forward pass for GLES3x (its pass is target 2.0), never for Direct3D 11.

gate: re-measure the actors acceptance (docs/waveC/actors/tools/measure.py) and this package's packet acceptance (docs/waveC/biome-electric-liquid/tools/packet_measure.py) on the final build with a pinned human color; the electric chevron cap requested by actors is in (shape 2 fill capped at 0.8 linear, 0 bright pixels around the chevron on my build).

gate: confirm the perfslope numbers on a quiet machine ('pwsh -NoProfile -File tools/verify.ps1 -Steps perfslope -ProbeExe Build/<final>/PainterIO.exe -Agent gateC'); on this wave's shared machine my build measured liquid 2.48, fire 2.69, electric 2.43 and the Gate B build liquid 2.24, fire 4.77, electric 3.14 ms per Mpix (docs/waveC/biome-electric-liquid/perf/).
